notes: Summary: DevLynx builds an IDE copilot (VSCode + JetBrains) focused on instant inline completions and long-form code generation. Primary ask: sub-150ms TTFT for single-line completion, consistent streaming for multi-line suggestions, fine-grained token budget control to avoid over-generation in editor UX.
Customer constraints: must run over VPC with SAML SSO and strict audit/log retention. Procurement leans toward Dedicated for predictable latency; open to Hosted for initial smoke tests.
TTFT targets: internal spec -> 50-120ms first token for inline completions (95th pct), 200ms tail for multi-line streaming. Customer quote: "cannot tolerate spikes >200ms — dev experience breaks".

Technical needs: model/version pinning to freeze behaviors for released copilots; token budget tuning per suggestion type (inline vs snippet vs whole-file); backpressure handling in extension (client-side queue + cancelation signals).

Performance experiments done so far: 2026-01-20 call — demo of hosted streaming (g4 instance) showed median TTFT ~180ms, high jitter on cold starts. 2026-02-10 lab run — batching increased throughput but added 40-70ms tail during bursts.

POC plan agreed 2026-02-25: 7-day Dedicated run on Redwood nodes, synthetic dev workload (200 active editors, 60% inline completions), measure TTFT 50/95/99 pct, jitter, token spend per session. SE to run cancellation/backpressure scenarios and log client buffer behavior.

Integration notes: VSCode extension uses a streaming websocket; need backpressure headers and recommendation for chunk size and idle-timeout. Prefers server-side prefix caching for common project headers to shave 20-40ms.
Security & compliance: engineering wants KMS integration and per-customer audit logging. Legal requested sample DPA and residency guarantees for EU customers (future expansion).
Commercial: looking at Dedicated reserved capacity 12-month commit if POC meets TTFT and token spend targets. Preliminary ARR band 50k-150k.
